newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Caltex Sri Lanka advances oil-blending plan.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Sri Lanka advances oil-blending plan.

text.p: Multinational oil giant Caltex has completed the first stage of blending premium quality oils at its Sri Lankan subsidiary, Lanka Lubricants, a local company official said on Wednesday.

"With the island-wide launch of locally blended diesel engine oil Delo on Monday, we have completed stage one of blending Caltex premium brands locally," said Lanka Lubricants general manager Ron Hopkins.
Hopkins said the diesel engine oil will enhance the company's bottom line. Diesel oil is the top-selling engine oil in Sri Lanka, where diesel vehicles outnumber petrol vehicles by threefold.
The company launched a premium engine oil for petrol vehicles - Havoline - in May.
The second stage of the company's blending plans will involve production of transmission and gear fluid next year.

Hopkins said net profits for the nine months to September 30, 1996, were marginally lower at 99.39 million rupees, down from 102.31 million rupees in the same period in 1995 due to "upfront costs of launching Havoline and Delo falling into the third quarter".
The company is on target for a net profit of 153 million rupees in 1996, up from 142 million in 1995, says Channa Kurukulasuriya, head of research at brokerage Lanka Securities.
Hopkins said upgrading the Lanka Lubricants factory to blend Havoline and Delo cost 160 million rupees.
The company estimates a further 40-50 million rupees will be spent on blending efficiency, marketing and distribution.
Formerly a state firm, Lanka Lubricants was privatised with the sale of a 51 percent stake to Caltex in 1992.
Caltex is a joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
The company was listed on the stock exchange in late September after issuing 11.7 million shares or 39 percent at 50 rupees. The shares last traded at 45 rupees on November 19.
